subject: Islamic Studies
board: TGA Islamic Studies scheme (aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, hadith, akhlaq)
source: Drive: RE folder and Islamic Studies schemes folder checked (Edexcel Int. GCSE Islamic Studies spec and KS4 SOW only; no KS3 Islamic material) - adapted to the TGA Islamic Studies scheme and the Edexcel spec content areas (1.4, 1.8, 2.2, 2.3, 2.6, 2.7), own knowledge, authentic sources only

lessons.unit: Unit 1: The Pillars of Iman in depth
lessons.title: Belief in the angels
objectives: Explain what Muslims believe about angels
Describe the roles of Jibril, Mikail, Israfil and the angel of death
Explain how belief in angels affects behaviour

keywords.def: angels: beings of light who obey Allah completely
the angel who brings revelation
the noble recording angels
the unseen

starter: Name the six pillars of iman.
What is the shahadah?
Why do Muslims believe in things they cannot see?

teach.heading: Angels in Islam
bullets: Created from light (Sahih Muslim, Aisha)
They obey Allah and never disobey (66:6)
They do not eat, sleep or tire
Belief in them is the second pillar of iman
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Aisha reported that the Prophet ﷺ said angels were created from light, jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam from what has been described to you (Muslim). Qur’an 66:6 says the angels do not disobey Allah in what He commands and do what they are commanded. Misconception: angels are not female, not partners of Allah, not to be worshipped or called upon.

teach.heading: Four angels and their roles
bullets: Jibril: revelation to the prophets
Mikail: rain and provision
Israfil: will blow the trumpet
The angel of death takes souls (32:11)
teach.note: Jibril and Mikail are named in Qur’an 2:97-98 (Edexcel passage). The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril in his true form with a vast creation covering the horizon (Bukhari and Muslim). Israfil is named in authentic hadith as the one who will blow the Trumpet (for example in the supplication of the Prophet ﷺ in Muslim). Keep descriptions simple.

teach.heading: Angels who record and protect
bullets: “Over you are noble recording angels” (82:10-12)
They write down every deed
They also guard people by Allah’s command (13:11)
teach.note: Ask: how would you behave if a record of every deed were being kept? (It is: that is reality.) Emphasise the hopeful side: good deeds are multiplied. Avoid frightening pupils; talk of accountability with mercy.

teach.heading: Effects of belief
bullets: Taqwa: awareness that deeds are recorded
Love for the angels who ask forgiveness for believers (40:7)
Strength: Allah helped believers with angels at Badr (3:124-125)
teach.note: Connect to next week’s battle of Badr. Pupils write two sentences: ‘Belief in angels makes me ...’. Close by sending salam on the angels.

practice: Match each angel to their role.
Quote or paraphrase 82:10-12.
What is a misconception about angels that Islam corrects?
independent: Create a fact file on Jibril using the Qur’an and Sunnah only.
Write a paragraph on how belief in the recording angels can shape behaviour.
Design a Venn diagram comparing angels and humans.
exit: What are angels created from?
Give one effect of believing in angels.
lessons.homework: Write six sentences about the angels with one Qur’an reference.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: matching cards with pictures; stretch: evaluate whether belief in unseen things is reasonable.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: The Pillars of Iman in depth
lessons.title: Belief in the revealed books
objectives: Name the revealed books and the prophets they came to
Explain why the Qur’an is the final, preserved book
Describe how the Qur’an was compiled

keywords.def: revealed to Musa (peace be upon him)
revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him)
revealed to Isa (peace be upon him)
the written, bound copy of the Qur’an

starter: Name two angels and their jobs.
What are the Kiraman Katibin?
How many pillars of iman are there?

teach.heading: A chain of revelation
bullets: Suhuf (scrolls) of Ibrahim
Tawrah to Musa
Zabur to Dawud
Injil to Isa
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Qur’an 4:163 (Edexcel passage) names Ibrahim, Isma’il, Is’haq, Ya’qub, Isa, Ayyub, Yunus, Harun, Sulayman and the Zabur to Dawud. Muslims believe the original revelations came from Allah and that the core message was Tawhid; Muslims do not claim that the present books are exactly the original revelation. Say this respectfully.

teach.heading: The Qur’an: final and preserved
bullets: Revealed to Muhammad ﷺ over about 23 years
“We have sent down the Reminder and We will guard it” (15:9)
It confirms and guards what came before (5:48)
teach.note: Link ‘guardian’ to 5:48: the Qur’an is the criterion. Ask: what does it mean that a book is ‘preserved’? Memorisation and writing both protected it.

teach.heading: Compiling the Qur’an
bullets: Revelation was memorised and written during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime
After Yamamah, Abu Bakr had the pages gathered
Zayd ibn Thabit led the team
Uthman copied standard manuscripts and sent them to cities
teach.note: This is narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (Zayd ibn Thabit). Umar suggested the collection as many reciters were killed at Yamamah. Zayd checked each verse against written copies and memorisers. Uthman’s copies unified the recitation. Ask: why was this careful method used?

teach.heading: Living with the Qur’an
bullets: Recite with tajwid
Understand the meaning
Act on its teachings
Teach it to others
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said the best of you is he who learns the Qur’an and teaches it (Bukhari, Uthman). Ask pupils for a goal: learn a new surah, understand a surah, apply a lesson.

practice: Match each book to its prophet.
Why is the Qur’an described as preserved?
Who led the compilation under Abu Bakr?
independent: Create a timeline of how the Qur’an was recorded.
Write 100 words: ‘Why Muslims believe in all the revealed books but follow the Qur’an’.
Make a revision card with four facts on Uthman’s copies.
exit: Name the book revealed to Dawud.
Who gathered the Qur’an after Yamamah?
lessons.homework: Memorise 15:9 and write a short explanation of what it means.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: timeline strips; stretch: explain why the compilation under Abu Bakr and Uthman matters.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: The Pillars of Iman in depth
lessons.title: Belief in the messengers
objectives: Explain why prophets were sent
Describe key prophets and their messages
Explain the meaning of Seal of the Prophets

keywords.def: prophet
messenger with a revealed scripture or law
protected by Allah from major sin and from wrongly conveying the message
Seal of the Prophets

starter: Name the book revealed to Isa.
Who compiled the Qur’an under Abu Bakr?
What does preserved mean?

teach.heading: Why prophets?
bullets: To call people to worship Allah alone (16:36)
To teach how to live
To be examples of character
To give good news and warnings
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Ask: if you wanted to know how to cook a new recipe, would a book be enough, or would you like a teacher? Prophets show us how to apply revelation.

teach.heading: Prophets in the Qur’an
bullets: Adam, Nuh and Ibrahim
Musa, Dawud and Isa
25 are named in the Qur’an
We believe in all of them without distinction (2:285)
teach.note: Give brief profiles. Ibrahim: stood for Tawhid and built the Ka’bah with Isma’il. Musa: led his people from oppression. Isa: born miraculously to Maryam; a servant and messenger of Allah (4:171). Muslims love and honour all prophets and say ‘peace be upon him’.

teach.heading: Their qualities
bullets: Truthfulness
Trustworthiness
Conveying the message
Intelligence and wisdom
teach.note: Ask: why must prophets be truthful and trustworthy? (Otherwise people could not rely on them.) These are classical qualities discussed by scholars. Prophets are human and do not share in Allah’s divinity (18:110).

teach.heading: The Seal of the Prophets
bullets: “Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets” (33:40)
No prophet after him
His message is for all humankind (34:28)
We follow his Sunnah
teach.note: Edexcel 1.3 passage. Draw out: the Qur’an was preserved, so no new revelation is needed. Misconception: that finality means earlier prophets are less important. Ask: why do Muslims say ‘peace and blessings be upon him’?

practice: Write three reasons Allah sent prophets.
Name four prophets and one thing about each.
Explain what ‘Seal of the Prophets’ means.
independent: Create a comparison chart of Ibrahim, Musa and Isa with their challenges and lessons.
Write a paragraph on why prophets had to be role models.
Prepare a short talk for a school assembly: ‘All the prophets, one message’.
exit: What was the main message of all the prophets?
Which verse says Muhammad ﷺ is the last prophet?
lessons.homework: Research one prophet from the Qur’an and write six facts with the Qur’an reference.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: prophet fact cards with images; stretch: explain the difference between a nabi and a rasul.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah - the road to Madinah
lessons.title: The Isra and Mi’raj
objectives: Describe the Night Journey and the Ascension
Explain the gift of the five daily prayers
Understand the significance of al-Aqsa

keywords.def: the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem
the ascension through the heavens
the blessed mosque in Jerusalem
the creature on which the Prophet ﷺ travelled

starter: Who was the Seal of the Prophets?
Name two things Ja’far told the Negus.
What do we call patience in Arabic?

teach.heading: A time of hardship
bullets: Khadijah and Abu Talib died within a short time
The Prophet ﷺ went to Ta’if and was rejected
Then Allah honoured him with the Night Journey
teach.note: Begin with bismillah and salawat. The year is called the ‘Year of Sorrow’ in the seerah. The Prophet ﷺ was driven out of Ta’if and made a heartfelt du’a (reported in the seerah). Ask: how does Allah comfort the sincere? Date: say it was in the Makkan period; scholars differ on the exact date.

teach.heading: The Night Journey
bullets: “Glory to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa” (17:1)
He led the prophets in prayer at al-Aqsa
He was taken on the Buraq
teach.note: Read 17:1 in English. Explain Buraq as mentioned in authentic hadith (Muslim, Anas) as a white animal smaller than a mule and bigger than a donkey. Ask: why is al-Aqsa special? (Qiblah for early Muslims, blessed land, linked with the prophets.)

teach.heading: The Ascension
bullets: He ascended through the seven heavens
He met prophets including Adam, Isa, Yusuf, Musa and Ibrahim
He was shown Paradise and the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim narrate that he met Adam in the first heaven, Yahya and Isa in the second, Yusuf in the third, Idris in the fourth, Harun in the fifth, Musa in the sixth and Ibrahim in the seventh. Ask: what message is in meeting so many prophets? (One message.)

teach.heading: The gift of salah
bullets: Fifty prayers were first prescribed
Musa advised him to ask for reduction
It became five prayers with the reward of fifty
Salah is a direct gift from Allah
teach.note: From Bukhari and Muslim (Anas, Malik ibn Sa’sa’ah). Stress mercy and ease. Ask: why did Allah make salah a gift given in the heavens rather than only by Jibril? (Shows its status.) Link to Y6 salah lesson.

teach.heading: Reactions and lessons
bullets: Quraysh mocked it; Abu Bakr affirmed it
Abu Bakr was called as-Siddiq, the truthful
Test of faith: trust the word of the Prophet ﷺ
teach.note: The story that Abu Bakr affirmed it is widely reported in the seerah. Ask: how can a believer respond to things that seem surprising? (By trusting authentic revelation and recognising Allah’s power.)

practice: What does Isra mean and what does Mi’raj mean?
Explain how the number of prayers changed from fifty to five.
Which verse describes the Night Journey?
independent: Create a poster showing the stages of the journey with the prophets met.
Write a paragraph: ‘Why is salah described as a gift?’
Write a short speech on why al-Aqsa is important to Muslims.
exit: What did Allah give the Muslims through the Mi’raj?
Which mosque was visited in the Isra?
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sequencing pictures of the stages; stretch: evaluate the importance of the event for the early Muslim community.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah - the road to Madinah
lessons.title: The Hijrah: plot, cave and journey
objectives: Retell the events of the Hijrah
Explain the roles of Abu Bakr, Ali, Asma and others
Explain why the Hijrah was a turning point

keywords.def: the migration of the Prophet ﷺ and Muslims from Makkah to Madinah
the emigrants from Makkah
the cave where the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid
trust in Allah

starter: What gift was given at the Mi’raj?
Why did Abu Bakr get the title as-Siddiq?
What does Isra mean?

teach.heading: The pledges at Aqabah
bullets: People of Yathrib accepted Islam
They pledged to protect the Prophet ﷺ
Mus’ab ibn Umayr taught them the Qur’an
Muslims began to migrate to Yathrib
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Explain that Yathrib became Madinah. Mus’ab was sent as a teacher and his da’wah was successful. Ask: why was a peaceful, welcoming city so important to the Muslims?

teach.heading: The plot to kill him
bullets: Quraysh leaders gathered to plot
They chose men from every tribe to strike together
Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ
Ali slept in his bed to deceive them
teach.note: Qur’an 8:30 refers to the plot: ‘when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you... but Allah plans, and Allah is the best of planners.’ Ali risked his life. Ask: how did the trust (amanah) fit here? (Ali returned the people’s trusts.)

teach.heading: The cave of Thawr
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid in a cave for three nights
“Do not grieve; Allah is with us” (9:40)
Asma bint Abi Bakr brought food
Abdullah ibn Urayqit guided them by a coastal route
teach.note: The words ‘Do not grieve, indeed Allah is with us’ are in 9:40. Bukhari records Abu Bakr’s fear about the footprints and the Prophet’s reassurance. Asma’s bringing food (and the belt story) is in Bukhari. Ask: what does tawakkul look like when you are afraid?

teach.heading: Suraqah and the arrival
bullets: Suraqah chased them for the reward
His horse sank into the ground
He asked for safety and turned back
They reached Quba, then Madinah
teach.note: From Sahih al-Bukhari. Suraqah later accepted Islam. Ask pupils to compare the Quraysh plan with Allah’s plan. Misconception: the Hijrah was an escape; in fact it was a planned and organised migration with human effort plus trust in Allah.

teach.heading: Why the Hijrah matters
bullets: The Muslim community could practise freely
The Islamic calendar begins from Hijrah
It separated truth from falsehood
It rewarded sacrifice for faith
teach.note: Umar later chose the Hijrah as the start of the calendar. Remind them of the hadith of intentions on migration. Ask: what would you sacrifice for your faith?

practice: Put the Hijrah events in order.
What did the Prophet ﷺ say to Abu Bakr in the cave?
Give two roles of Ali and Asma.
independent: Create a map and timeline of the Hijrah.
Write the conversation in the cave between the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr using 9:40.
Write a paragraph: ‘Why was the Hijrah a turning point?’
exit: Name the cave where they hid.
Give one reason the Hijrah was important.
lessons.homework: Write a diary entry of Asma bint Abi Bakr during the three days.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: map with labels; stretch: assess whether the Hijrah was a defeat or a victory.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah - the road to Madinah
lessons.title: Madinah: mosque, brotherhood and a new society
objectives: Describe the welcome in Madinah
Explain the building of the mosque and the brotherhood
Evaluate the importance of the Ansar

keywords.def: the helpers of Madinah
the brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar
the Prophet’s Mosque in Madinah
the first mosque built in Islam

starter: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in the cave?
Who were the Muhajirun?
Name the guide of the Hijrah route.

teach.heading: The joyful welcome
bullets: Madinah welcomed the Prophet ﷺ with joy
He stayed at Quba and founded its mosque
His camel stopped where the Prophet’s Mosque was built
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Explain that the first thing he did was build a mosque, showing priorities. Qur’an 9:108 refers to the mosque founded on taqwa from the first day. Ask: why build a mosque first?

teach.heading: The Prophet’s Mosque
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ worked with the Companions to build it
It was a place for prayer, learning and meetings
It also housed the poor of the Muhajirun
Simple walls and palm trunks
teach.note: Link to Edexcel 1.4: building of mosques on arrival. Ask: what functions do mosques have today? How can your masjid serve the community?

teach.heading: Brotherhood
bullets: Muhajirun and Ansar were paired as brothers
Sa’d ibn ar-Rabi’ offered half his wealth to Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf
Abd ar-Rahman asked only to be shown the market
The Qur’an praises the Ansar (59:9)
teach.note: From Sahih al-Bukhari. Qur’an 59:9 says they prefer others over themselves even though they are in need. Ask: what is the difference between generosity and showing off? Compare with the dignity of Abd ar-Rahman.

teach.heading: A shared society
bullets: The community included Muslims and non-Muslim tribes
The early agreement set out rights and duties
Justice and defence were shared
teach.note: The document known as the Constitution or Charter of Madinah is recorded in early seerah sources. Say that historians study its details. Highlight the principle: the community protects all its members. Keep claims moderate.

teach.heading: Companions who supported the Prophet ﷺ
bullets: Abu Bakr: closest friend, first caliph
Umar: strong, just, second caliph
Uthman: generous, third caliph
Ali: brave, scholar, fourth caliph
teach.note: Edexcel 1.4e. These are the four Rightly Guided Caliphs. Give one story each: Abu Bakr gave all for the Hijrah; Umar’s conversion strengthened the Muslims; Uthman funded Tabuk and the well of Rumah; Ali slept in the Prophet’s bed. Ask: which quality do you most admire?

practice: What was the first building project in Madinah?
Explain the story of Sa’d and Abd ar-Rahman.
Match each caliph with a quality.
independent: Write a news report on the first Friday in Madinah.
Create an infographic: Muhajirun and Ansar.
Write a paragraph: ‘Why was brotherhood so important after the Hijrah?’
exit: Who were the Ansar?
Give one function of the Prophet’s Mosque.
lessons.homework: Interview a family member about what their local masjid does for the community.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: matching Companion cards; stretch: compare Madinan society before and after Islam.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah - the road to Madinah
lessons.title: The Battle of Badr
objectives: Explain why the Battle of Badr took place
Describe the main events and outcome
Evaluate its importance for the Muslim community

keywords.def: the first major battle between Muslims and Quraysh, Ramadan 2 AH
criterion between truth and falsehood
a leader of Quraysh who strongly opposed Islam
payment for the release of prisoners

starter: What is mu’akhah?
Name the four caliphs.
Where did the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hide?

teach.heading: Why Badr?
bullets: The Muslims had lost homes and property in Makkah
A Quraysh caravan led by Abu Sufyan passed near Madinah
The caravan escaped; the Quraysh army still marched
The two forces met at Badr
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Qur’an 22:39 gave permission to fight those who were wronged. Explain that the Muslims went out to intercept the caravan but Allah arranged a meeting with the army (8:7). Ask: why did Quraysh not return home once their caravan was safe? (Pride.)

teach.heading: The numbers
bullets: About 313 Muslims
About 1,000 Quraysh
Few horses and camels on the Muslim side
Quraysh had better weapons
teach.note: Numbers: around 313 Muslims and about 1,000 Quraysh are the common figures in the sources. Ask pupils to calculate the ratio: about 1:3. Qur’an 3:123: Allah gave you victory at Badr while you were weak.

teach.heading: The battle
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ prayed through the night
Battle began with duels, then a general fight
Allah sent angels in support (3:124-125)
Muslims won decisively
teach.note: Reports mention Abu Jahl was killed at Badr and 14 Muslims were martyred. Roughly seventy of the Quraysh were killed and seventy captured. Emphasise that figures are approximate in the sources. Ask: how does du’a combine with effort?

teach.heading: The prisoners
bullets: Prisoners were treated with kindness
Many were released for a ransom
Some literate prisoners taught Muslims to read
“They give food, for love of Allah, to the poor, orphan and captive” (76:8)
teach.note: Reports in the seerah record that the Muslims shared their food with the captives. The ‘teach ten Muslims to read’ ransom is reported in Ahmad and the seerah. Use ‘reports state’. Ask: what does this show about Islamic treatment of prisoners?

teach.heading: Why Badr mattered
bullets: The first great victory of the Muslims
Confidence and credibility grew
Quraysh were shaken but sought revenge
Called ‘Yawm al-Furqan’, the Day of Criterion (8:41)
teach.note: Edexcel 1.8: reasons and importance. Ask: how might a small community feel after Badr? Also: how did it increase tension with Quraysh (leading to Uhud)? Provide pupils with a framework: reasons, events, outcome, importance.

practice: Calculate the ratio of Muslims to Quraysh at Badr.
Give two reasons for the battle.
Why is Badr called the Day of Criterion?
independent: Write a battle report with a heading, reasons, events, outcome and importance.
Write a diary entry from a Muslim who fought at Badr.
Design a chart: Muslim treatment of prisoners and the lessons.
exit: When did the Battle of Badr take place (month and year AH)?
Give one result of the battle.
lessons.homework: Read 3:123-126 in English and write what it teaches about trust in Allah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: timeline strip and word bank; stretch: evaluate whether Badr was mostly a military or a moral victory.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh and the sources of Islamic law
lessons.title: The sources of Shari’ah
objectives: Name the main sources of Islamic law
Explain ijma and qiyas simply
Explain the importance of following the Qur’an and Sunnah

keywords.def: the path of Islamic guidance and law from Allah
agreement of the scholars on a ruling
analogy: applying a ruling to a similar new case
scholarly effort to reach a ruling

starter: Name the first two caliphs.
What is a hadith?
Why was the Qur’an compiled?

teach.heading: What is Shari’ah?
bullets: “We made for each a way” (5:48)
The path to Allah’s pleasure
Covers worship, character and dealings
Aims to protect life, faith, mind, family and wealth
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Edexcel 2.7 passage: 5:48. Note that Shari’ah is far wider than punishments. Ask: what rules guide a school? Compare with the purpose of Shari’ah: a guide for good.

teach.heading: The Qur’an and Sunnah
bullets: The Qur’an is the first source
The Sunnah explains and applies it
“Obey Allah and obey the Messenger” (4:59)
Example: the Qur’an orders salah; the Sunnah shows how
teach.note: Also mention 59:7: ‘Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids, abstain.’ Ask: what would we lose without the Sunnah? Give the example of how to pray or how to perform Hajj.

teach.heading: Ijma: consensus
bullets: Agreement of the scholars of a time on a ruling
Example: the compilation of the Qur’an in one book
It cannot contradict the Qur’an and Sunnah
teach.note: Keep it simple. The Prophet ﷺ said his Ummah would not agree upon misguidance (reported in Ibn Majah and elsewhere with varying grading; do not quote it as a precise text). Better: explain that scholars across time have agreed on core matters like the five prayers.

teach.heading: Qiyas: analogy
bullets: Applying a known ruling to a new, similar case
Needs the same reason (illah)
Example: drugs and alcohol, as both intoxicate
teach.note: Use the standard example: alcohol is forbidden because it intoxicates; scholars apply the same reason to other intoxicants. Ask pupils to think of a modern situation where scholars need to reason (new technology). Note that ordinary pupils do not make rulings; we ask qualified scholars.

teach.heading: Following with humility
bullets: We ask qualified scholars
“Ask the people of knowledge if you do not know” (16:43)
Scholars may differ in minor matters
We keep respect and unity
teach.note: Mention the four schools in brief (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi’i, Hanbali) as ways scholars systematised law; we will revisit in Year 9. Teach adab: no insulting people who follow another valid opinion.

practice: List the four sources of Shari’ah.
Explain qiyas using the alcohol example.
Why do we need the Sunnah as well as the Qur’an?
independent: Create a diagram with the four sources and an example for each.
Write a paragraph on why qualified scholars are needed to answer fiqh questions.
Write a short Q and A: ‘Why does Islam have a law?’
exit: Name the first two sources of Shari’ah.
What is qiyas?
lessons.homework: Ask a trusted adult for one example of a ruling taken from the Qur’an and one from the Sunnah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: source cards to sort; stretch: discuss why a source hierarchy is needed.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh and the sources of Islamic law
lessons.title: Halal, haram and the five rulings
objectives: Define halal and haram
Explain the five categories of rulings with examples
Apply the categories to everyday situations

keywords.def: obligatory: rewarded for doing, sinful for leaving
recommended: rewarded for doing, not sinful for leaving
permitted: neither rewarded nor sinful
disliked: better to avoid
forbidden: sinful to do

starter: Name the four sources of Shari’ah.
What is qiyas?
Where in the Qur’an is Shari’ah mentioned?

teach.heading: Halal and haram
bullets: “Eat of what is lawful and good on the earth” (2:168)
Halal: permitted; haram: forbidden
Allah permits what is good and forbids what is harmful
Most things are halal unless prohibited
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The principle that the default is permissibility is accepted in matters of dealings and food. Edexcel passage 5:3 lists forbidden meats. Ask: why does Allah forbid? (Protect us from harm.)

teach.heading: The five rulings
bullets: Fard: five daily prayers
Mustahabb: extra voluntary prayers
Mubah: choosing which halal meal to eat
Makruh: wasting water
Haram: lying, stealing, riba, alcohol
teach.note: This is the Ahkam pentad in the Edexcel spec. Note that Hanafis also distinguish wajib from fard; keep to the five categories. Use a number line from ‘must do’ to ‘must not do’. Ask pupils to place examples.

teach.heading: The doubtful matters
bullets: “The halal is clear and the haram is clear”
Between them are doubtful matters
Whoever avoids them protects his religion
Narrated by an-Nu’man ibn Bashir (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Explain with a practical example: a food product with an unfamiliar ingredient; check the label or ask someone knowledgeable. Ask: how can we avoid over-worry as well as carelessness?

teach.heading: Applying the categories
bullets: Pray Fajr: fard
Read extra Qur’an: mustahabb
Choose a blue or red bag: mubah
Gossip: haram
teach.note: Run a sorting game with real-life scenarios. Discuss edge cases (e.g. a game that wastes time: makruh? haram?). Stress that we refer complex issues to scholars.

practice: Place these in the five categories: eating halal chicken; praying Dhuhr; backbiting; fasting an extra Monday; wasting food.
Define halal and haram.
What should we do with doubtful matters?
independent: Create a ‘Five Rulings’ table with two examples each.
Write a paragraph on why Islam has categories of rulings.
Design a poster for food-label checking.
exit: Name the five categories of rulings.
Is a mubah action rewarded?
lessons.homework: List five things you do daily and categorise them with explanations.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with colours; stretch: explain the wisdom of having a middle category (mubah).

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh and the sources of Islamic law
lessons.title: Zakah: purifying wealth
objectives: Define zakah and explain its purpose
State the conditions and rate
Name the categories of those who receive zakah

keywords.def: obligatory yearly charity that purifies wealth
the minimum wealth on which zakah is due
one full lunar year
voluntary charity

starter: List the five rulings.
Is fasting in Ramadan fard or mustahabb?
Give an example of a mubah action.

teach.heading: What is zakah?
bullets: The third pillar of Islam
“Establish prayer and give zakah” (2:43)
It purifies wealth and the heart
It supports the poor and the community
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The word zakah means purification and growth. Ask: if wealth is a trust from Allah, what do we owe? Link to 9:103, which tells the Prophet ﷺ to take charity to purify them.

teach.heading: Who must pay and how much
bullets: Muslims who hold wealth above the nisab for a year
The rate is 2.5% on savings and gold or silver
The nisab is linked to 85 g of gold or 595 g of silver
Calculated on wealth after basic needs and debts
teach.note: Worked example: Aisha has £6,000 above the nisab for a full year. Zakah = 2.5% × 6,000 = £150. Say that tools such as the current nisab value should be checked with a trusted scholar or organisation because values change.

teach.heading: Who receives it
bullets: The poor and the needy
Zakah collectors
Those whose hearts are to be reconciled
Freeing slaves, those in debt, the cause of Allah, the traveller
teach.note: The eight categories come from 9:60 (Edexcel 3.4 passage). Ask: why is it forbidden to give zakah to the Prophet’s family? (To protect their dignity; mention only if asked.) Discuss how a society with zakah reduces poverty.

teach.heading: Zakat al-Fitr and sadaqah
bullets: Zakat al-Fitr: paid before the Eid prayer
Ibn Umar: one sa’ of food (Bukhari)
Sadaqah can be given any time
Even a kind word is charity
teach.note: Zakat al-Fitr purifies the fasting person and feeds the poor. Today it is often paid as money; scholars give the current amount. Ask for ways Year 8 pupils can give sadaqah.

teach.heading: The wisdom of giving
bullets: Reduces greed
Builds love between rich and poor
Protects wealth from misuse
“Charity does not decrease wealth” - hadith in Muslim
teach.note: The hadith ‘Charity does not decrease wealth’ is in Sahih Muslim (Abu Hurayrah). Ask pupils to explain how this can be true spiritually. Encourage a class charity project.

practice: Calculate zakah on £4,000 held above the nisab for a year.
List four categories of zakah recipients.
State one difference between zakah and sadaqah.
independent: Make a leaflet ‘Zakah explained’.
Calculate 2.5% of £800, £2,400 and £10,000 and show your working.
Write a paragraph on why zakah is both worship and social justice.
exit: What is the rate of zakah on savings?
Name two categories who can receive it.
lessons.homework: Plan a charity action for the school community and explain how it follows Islamic teaching.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: calculation steps on cards; stretch: explain why zakah is not the same as taxes.

lessons.title: Hadith: the believers are like one body
objectives: Explain the hadith of the body and the hadith on brotherhood
Link them to Muslim unity and compassion
Apply them to school and community

keywords.def: brotherhood and sisterhood in faith
mercy and compassion
the global Muslim community
mutual mercy

starter: What is zakah?
Name one category of zakah recipient.
Why did the Ansar welcome the Muhajirun?

teach.heading: One body
bullets: “The believers in their mutual love and mercy are like one body”
“When one part is in pain, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever”
Narrated by an-Nu’man ibn Bashir (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Ask: when you stub a toe, who feels it? The whole person. Likewise, we feel for others’ pain. Link to current events: Muslims who suffer in different parts of the world. Encourage action: du’a, giving, awareness.

teach.heading: A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim
bullets: “He does not wrong him or hand him over”
Allah helps the one who helps his brother
Narrated by Ibn Umar (Bukhari, Muslim)
Qur’an: “The believers are but brothers” (49:10)
teach.note: Full hadith: a Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he does not wrong him or abandon him. Whoever fulfils his brother’s need, Allah fulfils his need; whoever removes a hardship, Allah removes a hardship from him on the Day of Judgment. Ask pupils to give practical examples at school.

teach.heading: How to live it
bullets: Greet with salam
Help in need
Forgive and settle disputes (49:9-10)
Pray for each other
teach.note: Role play: two pupils disagree about a game; one applies 49:10. Show the steps of making peace: listen, apologise, forgive, restore. Link to Y6 love for your brother what you love for yourself.

teach.heading: Brotherhood beyond differences
bullets: Muslims come from many races and nations
“The most noble of you is the one with most taqwa” (49:13)
Racism and pride are rejected
teach.note: Edexcel 2.8 passage 49:11-13. Mention the Prophet’s farewell sermon later (Y9). Ask: what steps can a school take to include everyone?

practice: Explain the ‘one body’ hadith in your own words.
Give three ways to help a classmate who is struggling.
What does 49:10 say about believers?
independent: Create a comic strip showing the ‘one body’ hadith in a school setting.
Write a paragraph: ‘What does brotherhood mean for the Ummah today?’
Plan a small act of service you will do this week and explain the hadith behind it.
exit: What does ‘one body’ mean in the hadith?
Give one rule of brotherhood from the hadith of Ibn Umar.
lessons.homework: Do one act of help for someone at home and write what you learned.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: comic template; stretch: link the hadith to the story of the Ansar and Muhajirun.

lessons.title: Akhlaq: truthfulness and avoiding lies
objectives: Explain the hadith on truthfulness and lying
State the signs of hypocrisy in the hadith
Apply honesty to school and online life

keywords.def: truthfulness
lying
hypocrisy: showing faith outwardly while hiding disbelief or insincerity
trust

starter: Explain the one body hadith.
What does 49:10 say?
Name a good manner shown to a neighbour.

teach.heading: Truthfulness leads to Paradise
bullets: “Truthfulness leads to righteousness”
“Righteousness leads to Paradise”
“A man keeps being truthful until he is written truthful with Allah”
Narrated by Ibn Mas’ud (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The same hadith warns that lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire; a man keeps lying until he is written as a liar with Allah. Ask: how does one small lie lead to another? Use a school example.

teach.heading: Signs of the hypocrite
bullets: When he speaks, he lies
When he promises, he breaks it
When trusted, he betrays
Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Explain nifaq (hypocrisy in action) and that this hadith warns of traits to avoid; it does not mean we label individuals. Ask: which of the three traits do people find hardest to avoid? Discuss how to repair broken trust.

teach.heading: Honesty in modern life
bullets: Do not cheat in exams
Do not share fake news or false quotes
Keep promises to friends and family
Admit mistakes and say sorry
teach.note: Link to hadith checking and online speech. The Prophet ﷺ taught that it is enough lying for a person to speak about everything he hears (Muslim, Abu Hurayrah). Ask: what should you do before forwarding a message?

teach.heading: Building a truthful character
bullets: Keep the company of the truthful (9:119)
Remember Allah is watching
Speak good or keep silent
Make du’a for a truthful tongue
teach.note: Qur’an 9:119: ‘O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful.’ Pupils set personal honesty goals and share. Close with revision of the half-term and a short quiz.

practice: Complete the chain: truthfulness leads to ______ which leads to ______.
Give an example of breaking a promise and how to repair it.
Why is sharing unchecked news a form of lying?
independent: Write a short story where a pupil tells the truth when it is hard.
Make a poster of the three signs of hypocrisy with positive opposites.
Write a plan to build honesty in your daily life.
exit: State the three signs of hypocrisy from the hadith.
What does 9:119 tell believers?
lessons.homework: Write a short apology or promise-repair letter for a real situation, or keep an honesty log for three days.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with pictures; stretch: discuss when honesty is difficult and how to be both truthful and kind.
